content: 1. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of calcium acetate in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, leading to decreased calcium acetate levels. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, ferrous fumarate enhances the GI absorption of calcium acetate, increasing its levels. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 2. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, ferrous fumarate increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing its GI absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 3. Calcium chloride reduces ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, ferrous fumarate increases calcium chloride levels by enhancing its GI absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 4. Calcium citrate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, ferrous fumarate increases calcium citrate levels by enhancing its GI absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 5. Calcium gluconate reduces ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, ferrous fumarate increases calcium gluconate levels by enhancing its GI absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 6. Ferrous fumarate decreases carbidopa levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Danazol increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Didanosine reduces ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, specifically didanosine chewable tablets and oral solutions. It is recommended to administer ferrous fumarate two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Gymnema reduces ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of tizanidine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Vitamin E reduces ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Acetohydroxamic acid decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Acitretin reduces the effects of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This interaction is contraindicated, and alternative methods of contraception should be used. 22. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 23. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Aluminum hydroxide reduces ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Ethinylestradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Amobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and the use of nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 28. Amoxicillin and ampicillin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 30. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to contraceptive failure, and alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraception should be used. 31. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract, leading to decreased absorption. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 32. Belzutifan reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm.
